newsitem.title: GREECE: UPDATED PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - SEPT 12.
newsitem.headline: UPDATED PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - SEPT 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek press:
ELEFTHEROTYPIA

--ICAP poll gives PASOK a two point lead over New Democracy, 31.9 to 29.9. The poll confirms the gains of smaller parties at the expense of PASOK and ND: Political Spring 6.2, DHKKI 5.5, Communists 4.9 and Left Coalition (Synaspismos) 4.8. Significant number undecided (4.5) or not replying (4.5).
Soundbites from yesterday's campaign trail
Evert- 'We believe in popular capitalism'.
Samaras - 'I would have landed on Imia'.
Communists - 'Simitis drops the mask of moderniser'
Tsovolas - 'No post-election collaboration with anyone'
TA NEA

--PASOK's six-point foreign policy programme, announced by Simitis yesterday, sets off a volley of statements and counter-statements between Evert, Simitis, and Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos. Simitis said Evert's seven proposals for foreign policy did nothing but confuse the issues. ND charged Simitis refused to draft a national strategy for national issues, implying that PASOK had "entered into commitments abroad". Statements by Evert referring to the three dead in the Imia crisis and last month's killing of two Greek Cypriots in the UN buffer zone drew the wrath of Pangalos, who said the memory of the five men should not be used for petty political purposes.
KATHIMERINI
--New poll confirms two major parties running neck and neck.

New Democracy (28.84 percent) leading PASOK (27.33).The DIMEL poll confirms previous poll results that ND supporters are rallying round but that PASOK is losing voters to smaller left parties, which look likely to be represented in Parliament - Communist Party 6.80, Left Coalition (Synaspismos) 5.29 and Democratic Social Movement (DHKKI) 5.48. Political Spring has 5.15 percent. Significant number of voters (10.98) still undecided, including 14.4 percent previous PASOK voters. Other polls show PASOK leading ND by a slim margin of 31.2 percent to 28.6 (Research International) DHKKI came in third with 4.7, followed by Synaspismos and Communists both with 4.4 percent and Political Spring with 3.6.
--56 percent said economic issues were the decisive factor in deciding how they would vote. National issues decided the matter for 24.24 percent, with social issues third with 12.62 per cent.
--Quibbling between Simitis and Evert camps on which journalists can address tomorrow's televised debate.
--Simitis and Evert disagree on tactics on national issues. The goals are the same, but how to get there is a point of dissension. Simitis says Evert's proposals "dangerous".
--Parties condemn snap decision by education ministry to increase number of university admissions as "vote-buying".
--Oil prices mark highest levels in six years, following new tension in Iraq. Local prices up slightly at midnight.
--Bank of Greece says policy on drachma is for stability, not overvaluation.

--Telecoms organisation (OTE) search for technical consultant on constructing telecoms network, and digital and other systems valuations, extended abroad. Bell Core, EDI (U.S.) and Analysis (U.K.) in the running. Decision expected after September 22 poll.
--Evert pledges cheaper power for residents in border regions.
IMERISIA
--Message from Brussels on New Democracy plans to revise convergence programme: EU officials say new changes would be pointless.
--34 billion drachma public debt a major headache for the new state budget.
--Trials on new natural gas pipeline begin on Monday. Network to begin operating in two months time.
EXPRESS
-- New decrease in interest rates on state titles possible, sources say, in event of majority government and if inflation does not worsen.
--Foreign capital inflow to stock exchange bolsters trading.
KERDOS
--Both major parties aim to bolster stock exchange. New tax breaks to encourage long-term investors expected.
--Athens public transport organisation (OASA) gets 10 billion drachma loan from group of 11 foreign and domestic banks.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Simitis reveals five-year 486 billion drachma plan to turn Crete into regional economic and development centre.
--Evert pledges support of small and medium-size enterprises, says will abolish 35 percent corporate tax and objective tax criteria.
--Automatic fines for EU countries not meeting criteria for economic and monetary union, Brussels decides.
--Banks allowed to issue letters of credit in foreign exchange for procurements by the state.
